name: Converted — Campaigns Agent Team
description: Talk with nine marketing agents — Otto, Piper, Cash, Iris, Ray, Milo, Penn, Vera, Cam — who watch, propose, and (with your approval) optimize your ad campaigns on Converted. Ask questions in plain language; approve changes in-conversation.

scopes.funnels:read: Read funnels, metrics, and agent proposals
scopes.agents:chat: Converse with the agent team (spends org AI credits)
scopes.agents:approve: Approve/dismiss agent proposals (mutates live ad accounts)

skills.name: Talk with the funnel team
skills.description: Group conversation with all nine agents — Otto (experiments), Piper (pages), Cash (budgets & campaigns), Iris (audiences), Ray (publishing), Milo (creative), Penn (copy), Vera (analytics), Cam (funnel structure). The most relevant agent answers each turn, attributed by name.
examples: How is my webinar funnel doing this week?

skills.name: Talk with a specific agent
skills.description: One-on-one with a named agent: ask Vera for numbers, Cash for budget moves, Otto for split tests, Iris for retargeting audiences. Send a DataPart {agent: <roster key>} to pin the persona; attribution is server-enforced.
examples: Cash, shift budget toward whichever campaign converts cheapest
Otto, is the pricing page worth testing?

skills.name: Review the team's proposals
skills.description: List pending agent proposals (budget rebalances, audience syncs, split tests) with full payload detail — the same queue shown in the in-app Command Center.

skills.name: Approve or dismiss a proposal
skills.description: Approve (executes, respecting org autonomy AND governance rules — a resource an admin has locked can't be executed by any agent even with an approval) or dismiss a pending proposal, in-conversation. Most proposals mutate the live ad account; the confirmation round-trip states exactly what each one does. Requires agents:approve and an explicit confirmation round-trip.

skills.name: Funnel overview
skills.description: List funnels; get a funnel's graph, stage metrics, leaks, and pending publish queue — the raw data behind the agents' answers.
